q_orientation.text: Assess mental status: Does the patient appear oriented ?

a_check_vitals.text: Check the patient’s vital parameters using the monitoring panel (heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation).

q_vitals_hr.text: Based on the monitoring panel: is the heart rate within an acceptable range for this patient?

options.label: Critically abnormal (tachycardia/bradycardia with concern for shock or instability)

q_vitals_rr.text: Based on the monitoring panel and observed breathing: is the respiratory rate and pattern acceptable?

options.label: Within normal range and breathing appears adequate
Mildly abnormal (increased or decreased rate but no immediate failure)
Critically abnormal (very high/low rate or signs of respiratory failure)

q_vitals_spo2.text: According to the pulse oximeter: is the oxygen saturation acceptable for this patient?

options.label: Mildly reduced but not immediately critical
Critically low saturation indicating severe hypoxia

q_vitals_bp.text: Based on the blood pressure readings and clinical impression: is the circulation (blood pressure and perfusion) acceptable?

options.label: Blood pressure and perfusion appear acceptable
Mildly abnormal (borderline low or high, but patient appears stable)
Critically abnormal (hypotension or hypertensive crisis with concern for shock or organ damage)

a_emergency_management.text: One or more vital signs are in a critical range. Focus on immediate life-saving treatment and rapid transport. Do not spend time on detailed history; ask only very brief questions if they change management.

a_airway_check.text: Check airway and measure respiratory rate.
